episodes.title: Trusting God Without Seeing the Whole Plan | Joshua Watson (Testimony) | EP #88 (Pt 3)
episodes.description:
Joshua Watson knew God had given him gifts. He wanted to understand what God wanted him to do with them.

In Part 3 of his testimony, Joshua shares his search for purpose, a powerful experience with God, and an unexpected calling. While worshiping in his workshop, God gave him a sense of peace about a future he still didn’t fully understand. Later, a story written for a Bible study became the beginning of something he hadn’t planned. As one step led to another, he began seeing how God was using the experiences he already had. The work was growing beyond what he could manage alone, and following God meant moving forward without knowing every turn ahead.

This is a story about finding purpose in what God has given us and learning to trust Him before we can see the whole plan.

▶ Pt 1 - https://youtu.be/JlPmYENgJDM

episodes.title: When Confidence is Control, and Control is Self-Defense | Joshua Watson (Testimony) | EP #87 (Pt 2)
episodes.description:
Joshua Watson thought he was confident—but control was really a mechanism he wielded was a way to protect himself from being hurt.

In Part 2 of his testimony, Joshua recounts his pursuit of a music career, the pride behind his decisions, and a turning point with God. He had a plan for his life and little room for anyone who questioned it. When a sermon challenged his choices, he found reasons to dismiss it. But when his own plans stopped working, he became willing to listen. He asked God for wisdom, and over time, God began changing how he saw himself and treated the people he loved. He had spent years insisting on his own way. Now he was learning how to serve.

This is a story about the control we mistake for confidence and what begins to change when we finally let God lead.

episodes.title: Thinking You Know the Bible Without Reading It | Joshua Watson (Testimony) | EP #86 Pt 1
episodes.description:
Joshua Watson thought he knew the Bible well enough to judge the preacher—without reading it for himself.

In Part 1 of his testimony, Joshua recounts his parents’ divorce, a reunion with his father, and the pride behind his certainty. Reconnecting with his dad filled a hole he hadn’t known was there, and he credits God with how a short visit became a lasting reunion. He listened closely to his father’s lessons about the Bible. But when he went to church, he was measuring the sermon against what he thought he knew. He believed God had something for him. He also believed he already had the answers.

This is a story about the things we miss when we’re sure we have nothing left to learn.

episodes.title: Nikki Casanova: Hoping You Belong but Fearing Your Past is Too Much (Testimony) | EP #85 (Pt 4)
episodes.description:
True healing doesn't erase the wreckage of the past—it gives us the strength to finally walk back through it.

In the final part of her testimony, Nikki Casanova explores the vulnerability of walking into a church community as a new believer and the tension of learning to be fully known. As her sobriety deepens and she begins pouring her time into serving others, a heavy conviction takes hold—pushing her to finally stop running and face the unresolved consequences of her past with a completely clear mind.   

This is a story about the true cost of accountability, the unexpected ways God redeems our darkest chapters, and the profound beauty of a fully restored life. 

▶ Pt 1 - https://youtu.be/LRHHbm1B1zY
▶ Pt 2 - https://youtu.be/lvkmTiKfTvU
▶ Pt 3 - https://youtu.be/HNAiKSjj2eM
_________

Portfolio Resident Services (PRS) is a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization dedicated to improving the quality of life for individuals, families, and senior citizens living in affordable housing communities.   

Operating across hundreds of properties, PRS provides critical on-site support through their "Good Neighbor Program". They focus on practical, skills-based assistance, offering resources like scholastic tutoring, after-school programs, financial literacy classes, and life skills training. Their core mission is grounded in community building—equipping residents with the knowledge, support, and actionable tools they need to maximize their potential and achieve lasting stability.

For further information, head over to their site at https://prspurpose.org.
